chunks: He who does a good deed will receive ten times its worth; and he who does evil will be requited to an equal degree; and no one will be wronged.
ai.seo_question: How does God reward good and bad deeds according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-An'am is often interpreted to highlight the asymmetry in divine generosity, where a single good deed yields tenfold reward while a sin incurs only its equivalent, underscoring God's mercy over strict retribution. The phrase 'they are not wronged' is understood to mean that the multiplier applies to the good deeds of the believers, ensuring that no effort is lost in the divine accounting.
